WA-2025-HB2689.title: Concerning the working connections child care program.
WA-2025-HB2689.summary:
Working Connections Child Care Program Eligibility .

Eligibility for the WCCC program is modified so that income eligibility is maintained at 60 percent of the SMI, instead of increasing to 75 percent of the SMI beginning July 1, 2029, and 85 percent of the SMI (subject to funding) beginning July 1, 2031.

Working Connections Child Care Subsidy Rates .

Child care subsidy base rates are set at the seventy-fifth percentile of market, beginning July 1, 2027, for licensed or certified child care providers. Beginning with the 2028 MRS, for its survey results to inform future rates, a child care subsidy rate region must achieve a provider response rate that is at least 40 percent and also greater than the response rate for that region in the prior MRS. A minimum survey response rate of 65 percent must be achieved for a valid survey once a region achieves a 65 percent response rate.

The DCYF is prohibited from allowing child care providers to receive a child care subsidy rate that is different than the rate for the subsidy region in which the provider is located.

Working Connections Child Care Subsidy Payments .

The DCYF must adopt rules that allow child care providers to claim daily subsidy payments as follows:
• for a child who has attended for 16 or more days in a calendar month, a provider may claim payment for the full number of authorized days;
• for a child who has attended 9 to 15 days in a calendar month, a provider may claim payment for the full number of authorized days, or for 15 days, whichever is fewer; and
• for a child who has attended 1 to 8 days in a calendar month, a provider may claim payment for the full number of authorized days, or for 11 days, whichever is fewer.

Daily subsidy payments must be paid in half-day or partial-day rates, as established in rule, for a child authorized for and receiving half-day or partial-day care. The requirement that the DCYF pay child care providers prospectively based on when child care is expected to begin is repealed.

WA-2025-HB2711.title: Concerning transportation resources.
WA-2025-HB2711.summary:
Fuel Taxes .

Fuel taxes received attributable to the aggregated inflationary adjustments to the component tax rates are distributed in the same manner as the other 2025 increases in the motor fuel tax and special fuel tax rates.

Retail Sales and Use Taxes on Acquisitions of Luxury Vehicles, and Recreational Vessels .

The use tax bases for the luxury vehicle tax and recreational vessel tax are modified to align with the corresponding sales tax bases, prohibiting the value of any trade-in from being deducted from the measure of tax. Various technical updates are made.

Motor homes are exempted from the sales and use taxes on luxury vehicles for the period July 1, 2026, through December 31, 2026.

Several changes are made to the retail sales and use taxes on luxury vehicles. In the case of a lease requiring periodic payments, the tax may be remitted in equal periodic payments over the term of the lease. The exemptions available under the general retail sales and use tax to enrolled tribal members and to nonresidents are extended to the sales and use taxes on luxury vehicles. Motor vehicle dealers are exempt from penalties and interest on any unpaid tax due for the tax reporting periods through June 30, 2026.

Luxury Aircraft Tax .

The additional 10 percent luxury tax on non-commercial aircraft, which would otherwise take effect on April 1, 2026, is repealed in its entirety.

Aircraft Fuel Tax .

On November 1, 2026, the current aircraft fuel tax is increased from 18 cents per gallon to 25 cents per gallon. The 7 cent increase will be deposited into the newly established Sustainable Aviation Fuel Airport Infrastructure Account created in the state treasury.

Aircraft Registration Fee .

Beginning January 1, 2027, the annual aircraft registration fee is increased from $15 to $30. The aircraft registration fee is increased annually by 2 percent beginning January 1, 2028. Increased revenue from the fee increase must be deposited in the Sustainable Aviation Fuel Account.

Aircraft Excise Tax .

Beginning on January 1, 2026, annual excise taxes by aircraft type are raised by a range of $70 to $1,095, increasing excise taxes due to a range of $120 to $1,220, depending on aircraft type.

Beginning on January 1, 2028, the aircraft excise taxes are increased by 2 percent each year. The increased amount, including the 2 percent annual adjustment, is deposited into the Sustainable Aviation Fuel Account.

Commercial unpiloted aircraft systems are made subject to the annual aircraft excise tax.

Sustainable Aviation Fuel Airport Infrastructure Account .

The Sustainable Aviation Fuel Airport Infrastructure Account is created in the state treasury. Twenty-eight percent of the revenue collected from aircraft fuel taxes by the WSDOT must be deposited in this account. These funds are subject to appropriation and can be used only for activities at airports supporting sustainable aviation fuel infrastructure improvement and sustainable aviation fuel infrastructure…

WA-2025-SB6237.title: Concerning rental property disclosures of flooding history and flood risk.
WA-2025-SB6237.summary:
Under the RLTA, a landlord must disclose to tenants the following:
• that the property may be located in a special flood hazard area or an area of potential flooding;
• that the landlord's insurance does not cover the loss of the tenant's personal possessions, and that the tenant should consider purchasing renter's insurance and flood insurance to insure their possessions from loss due to fire, flood, or other risk of loss; and
• that information about hazards that may affect the property, including whether the property may be at risk of flooding, is available from the county government in which the property is located.

The disclosures required by the act only apply to leases entered into after December 31, 2026.

WA-2025-SB5346.title: Restricting mobile device usage by public school students.
WA-2025-SB5346.summary:
Digital Citizenship, Media Literacy, and Internet Safety. The definition of digital citizenship is revised to include that the norms of appropriate, responsible, and healthy behavior related to current technology use includes the use of mobile devices. "Mobile device" means any personal mobile telephone or other portable electronic communication device with which a user engages in a call or writes or sends a message, or any device in which the user plays a game or watches a video. Mobile device does not include school-issued devices.

In its web-based location to support digital citizenship, media literacy, and Internet safety, OSPI must include research on student use of mobile devices and recommended best practice strategies for teaching students how to use their mobile devices responsibly, such as research commissioned by the Washington Association of School Administrators, School Information Research Services.

Report on Student Use of Mobile Devices. By December 15, 2027, OSPI must submit a report with:
• a summary of the policies and procedures that have been adopted by public schools in Washington and in other states limiting student use of mobile devices during instructional hours;
• a summary of the barriers that public schools have experienced when implementing these policies and procedures;
• evidence-based recommendations related to student mobile device use during instructional hours that support academic learning, healthy social relationships and emotional well-being, and recommendations for incorporating student mobile device use within digital citizenship; and
• student input on the recommendations.

The Legislature intends to consider OSPI's recommendations with a goal of enabling every school district to implement a bell-to-bell cell phone policy that is tailored to the needs of their community by 2030.

Policies on Mobile Devices. School district boards of directors may adopt policies and procedures that limit the possession and use of mobile devices by students. When considering the adoption of policies and procedures, school district boards of directors are encouraged to review recommendations provided by OSPI.

WA-2025-SB6248.title: Addressing travel insurance.
WA-2025-SB6248.summary:
Washington Travel Insurance Act .

The Washington Travel Insurance Act is enacted.

Limited Lines Travel Insurance Producer License . The Insurance Commissioner (Commissioner) may issue a limited lines travel insurance producer license to an individual or business entity that has filed with the Commissioner an application for a limited lines travel insurance producer license in a form and manner prescribed by the Commissioner. The limited lines travel insurance producer must be licensed to sell, solicit, or negotiate travel insurance through an authorized insurer. No person may act as a limited lines travel insurance producer or travel insurance retailer unless properly licensed or registered, respectively. The grounds for the suspension, revocation, and penalties applicable to resident insurance producers apply to the limited lines travel insurance producers and travel retailers.

Travel Retailers. A travel retailer is a business entity that makes, arranges, or offers planned travel and may offer and disseminate travel insurance as a service to its customers on behalf of and under the direction of a limited lines travel insurance producer. A travel retailer may offer and disseminate travel insurance under a limited lines travel insurance producer business entity license only if specified requirements are met:
• The limited lines travel insurance producer or travel retailer must provide to purchasers of travel insurance: a description of the material terms of the insurance coverage; a description of the process for filing a claim; a description of the review or cancellation process for the travel insurance policy; and the identity and contact information of the insurer and limited lines travel insurance producer.
• At the time of licensure, the limited lines travel insurance producer must establish and maintain a register, on a form prescribed by the Commissioner, of each travel retailer that offers travel insurance on the limited lines travel insurance producer's behalf. The register must be maintained and updated by the limited lines travel insurance producer and must include the name, address, and contact information of the travel retailer and an officer or person who directs or controls the travel retailer's operations, and the travel retailer's federal tax identification number.
• The limited lines travel insurance producer must submit the register to the Commissioner annually in a form and manner prescribed by the Commissioner.
• The limited lines travel insurance producer must certify that the registered travel retailer complies with federal law related to c
rimes by or affecting persons engaged in the business of insurance whose activities affect interstate commerce
.

WA-2025-HB2348.title: Updating timber sale process efficiencies and adopting consistent language for the department's land sales.
WA-2025-HB2348.summary:
Procedures for notifying the public for land sales are modified. Notice of the sale of lands managed by DNR no longer has to be posted in conspicuous places in DNR's Olympia office or in the office of the county auditor, but must be posted on DNR's public website. The list of lands and the appraised values that DNR must produce for all land sales no longer needs to be in pamphlet form. The list should be made available prior to the date of the sale, including on the Internet. Clarifying language is added that lands acquired by escheat, deed of sale, gift or through the land bank may only be sold after appraisal and for at least fair market value, and the transaction is in the best interest of the state or affected trust.

The manner in which DNR must publicize the sale of valuable materials valued at $250,000 or less is modified. DNR may publicize valuable materials sales through the agency's website or through other methods deemed most practical by DNR. Valuable materials sales may take place either at DNR's applicable region headquarters or at an alternate location designated by DNR. DNR is no longer required to publicize such sales at DNR's Olympia office or at the office of the county auditor of the county in which the materials are located. DNR is no longer required to print a paper copy of the list of all valuable materials on public lands to be sold, but must make the list available upon request. A sale of valuable materials that has been offered, but for which no bids have been received, may be reoffered consistent with existing statutory requirements.

WA-2025-SB5720.title: Enacting the uniform consumer debt default judgments act.
WA-2025-SB5720.summary:
Complaint Requirements. Default judgments in consumer debt collection actions may be entered only if the complaint states specific information pertaining to the debt, the parties, and to the legal action.

If a plaintiff is bringing an action to recover purchased debt on behalf of a holder of purchased debt, additional information regarding the chain of ownership of the debt must be stated.

Specific documents must be attached to the complaint demonstrating the existence of the debt. Certain copies of documents must also be attached to the complaint depending on the type of debt being collected. Such documents must satisfy court rules and statutory requirements governing business records as evidence.

Consumer Notice Requirements. A consumer notice must be included in or accompany a complaint served on a consumer before a default judgment may be entered in a collection action for consumer debt. The notice must provide information on what may happen if a consumer does not respond to the complaint; the consequences of a default judgment; and information on seeking legal assistance.

A standard consumer notice form is provided.

Failure to Comply. A court may deny a plaintiff's motion for default judgment if the plaintiff fails to comply with the complaint and consumer notice requirements, unless the plaintiff submits an amended complaint that complies with such requirements.

The commission or facilitation of an act or practice in violation of the complaint and consumer notice requirements by a person who holds purchased debt or any affiliate is considered a violation of the Consumer Protection Act and will prevent such persons from recovering any interest, service charge, attorneys' fees, collection costs, delinquency charge, or any other fees or charges aside from the original claim or obligation.

Application. The act applies to default judgments in legal actions to collect on consumer debt. The act does not apply to actions to obtain or force a sale of real property or personal property, nor does it apply to actions to collect debts owed to state or local governments. WA-2025-SB6039.title: Modernizing methods of communications by the department of labor and industries.
WA-2025-SB6039.summary:
Communications. Specified notice and communication provisions across laws administered by L&I are updated. In the amended provisions, required notices, orders, citations, determinations, and similar communications may be provided using electronic delivery or a nonelectronic method. In specified contexts, the method must allow delivery to be tracked or confirmed. In some contexts, correspondence and notices sent electronically are considered received on the date sent, and certain time periods are adjusted to reflect electronic delivery.

The changes apply across multiple L&I administered programs, including contractor registration; trade licensing and enforcement; workplace safety and health enforcement; wage and hour enforcement; workers’ compensation and industrial insurance determinations and appeals; and safety programs for equipment subject to L&I inspection and enforcement.

Nonelectronic Option. Before using an electronic method for the first time under specified provisions, L&I must provide the affected party the option to receive communications through a nonelectronic method.

Conforming Changes. Conforming changes in related provisions are made, including updating certain terminology and converting some written numbers and dollar amounts to numerals.
WA-2025-SB6039.summarySource: Washington Legislature final bill report (6039-S SBR FBR 26, 2026-04-01)
